answer: The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. A bookbinder guild record with binding commission chain works as the gate: commissions bound for one bindery over years. The price is per head, and the sparrow test proves it: Each of 175 aliases needs its own commission chains, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The signal trail is public, the wharf check is cheap to run, and a farm of 175 aliases pays 175 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
